name: Ethnic/genetic fatalism ("genetics is everything")

lead: Ethnic or genetic fatalism, often phrased 'genetics is everything', is the belief that facial structure, height and ethnic background are set at birth and largely decide romantic and social outcomes. It frames how people in blackpill and looksmaxxing forums choose which changes are worth attempting, and some looksmaxxing communities have moved toward incremental improvement as a response.

Believers point to attractiveness hierarchies, hypergamy and dating-app data. Research confirms appearance effects in some settings, but how large or fixed they are is disputed, and critics say the underlying mating research is overgeneralised.

paras: It is a belief rather than a practice: people discuss it in forums and use it to decide where to put effort, from accepting traits as fixed to focusing on what can be changed such as skin, fitness, grooming and style.
Commentators link fatalistic belief with hopelessness, and some institutions describe associated incel communities as extremist.

angle.text: Blackpill and looksmaxxing forum posters use this framing to argue that facial structure, height and ethnicity set romantic outcomes, and it shapes which changes people decide to attempt. Attractiveness effects are studied; how fixed they are remains debated.

lead: Ethnic or genetic fatalism, often phrased 'genetics is everything', is the belief in blackpill and looksmaxxing communities that facial structure, height and ethnic background are fixed at birth and largely decide romantic and social outcomes. [1][2]

Grokipedia calls this 'genetic determinism' and says it holds that genetics, especially looks, mostly decide outcomes, with personality and effort mattering little; it adds that some looksmaxxing communities have moved partly away from this fatalism towards incremental improvement. [2] Wikipedia notes that looksmaxxing attributes sexual success to perceived genetic advantages. [3]

Researchers describing the blackpill portray it as the more nihilistic strand of incel ideology. Evidence that attractiveness effects exist is reported in some research, but its size and fixity are disputed. [1][4]

paras: Wikipedia says the black pill holds that looks and genetics fixed social hierarchy so that unattractive men cannot escape it, and lists 'just be white', the idea that white men face the fewest dating obstacles, among related ideas. [1]

On looksmax.org, one thread argues that teenage Asian males can only change their appearance during puberty and ties outcomes to ancestry and diet. Posts of this kind blend fatalism with hard and soft looksmaxxing advice.

Grokipedia reports that incels cite hypergamy and dating-app data to argue outcomes are fixed, and says the reasoning overgeneralises short-term mating research and ignores assortative mating and changing preferences. It also cites a 2023 study in which incels overestimated women's focus on looks and underestimated interest in kindness and loyalty. [4]

Wikipedia's lookism article reports that studies find attractive people receive more callbacks and perceived positive traits, with effects varying by job, country and gender, and that researchers disagree about their significance. [5]
